pr_body:

### What problem does this PR solve? <!--add issue link with summary if exists-->

Fix [14602](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/14602), and the same problem of `Apply`.

Always put Build side above Probe side.

### What is changed and how it works?

Mainly modify common_plans.go:
 - Add new argument "driverSide string" for function explainPlanInRowFormat() and prepareOperatorInfo().
 - Modify explainPlanInRowFormat()
     - Indicate driven side and driving side of parent plan.
     - Call prepareOperatorInfo() first with the Build side.
 - Modify prepareOperatorInfo(), append `driverSide` to `explainId`.

 Update test files.

 - Integration test

 - Has exported function/method change
 - Has persistent data change

issue_context.title: Show the driven side and driving side of `Join` and `IndexLookUpReader` in `EXPLAIN` result
issue_context.body:
This is an advice from DBAs.

Use `IndexLookUpReader` as a detailed example:
```
mysql> explain select * from t use index(idx);
+-------------------+----------+-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| id                | count    | task      | operator info                                                       |
+-------------------+----------+-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| IndexLookUp_6     | 10000.00 | root      |                                                                     |
| ├─IndexScan_4     | 10000.00 | cop[tikv] | table:t, index:a, range:[NULL,+inf], keep order:false, stats:pseudo |
| └─TableScan_5     | 10000.00 | cop[tikv] | table:t, keep order:false, stats:pseudo                             |
+-------------------+----------+-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
3 rows in set (0.00 sec)

mysql>
```
The above is the current explain result.
DBAs want to let it be
```
mysql> explain select * from t use index(idx);
+-------------------+----------+-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| id                | count    | task      | operator info                                                       |
+-------------------+----------+-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| IndexLookUp_6       | 10000.00 | root      |                                                                     |
| ├─IndexScan_4(Build)| 10000.00 | cop[tikv] | table:t, index:a, range:[NULL,+inf], keep order:false, stats:pseudo |
| └─TableScan_5(Probe)| 10000.00 | cop[tikv] | table:t, keep order:false, stats:pseudo                             |
+-------------------+----------+-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
3 rows in set (0.00 sec)

```
to show the execution logic more clearly.


For hash join, the side to build hash table is the `Build` side and the other is the `Probe` side.
For index join, the side to directly read data is the `Build` side, the other is the `Probe` side.
For merge join, though the two sides are the same in ideal case. In tidb's actual execution logic, it will read one side's data, then compare them with the other side. The first side is treated as `Build` side in explain.

review_comments: Why merge join has to differentiate the driver side?

"When MergeJoin is actually executed, there is a slight difference between left and right, and the outer join is more obvious."
It seems like DBAs have discussed this problem, refer to channel `team-sql-engine`.
